item.description: Understanding the mechanisms and predictability of biodiversity change I study how and why biodiversity changes across space and time. What determines where species occur, how their ranges and communities change, and whether they persist in a rapidly changing world? My research seeks to understand the ecological mechanisms underlying these dynamics, linking individual fitness, movement and species interactions to population and community dynamics and large-scale biodiversity patterns. In my research group, we integrate ecological theory, biodiversity observations and quantitative models to unravel the drivers of biodiversity change, investigate delayed ecological responses, and assess the vulnerability of species and communities to climate and land-use change.

item.title: Research themes
item.description: What determines where species occur, and how do their niches and ranges change through time? ... Species distributions are determined by the complex interplay of environmental constraints, species interactions, demography, dispersal and evolutionary history. We study how ecological niches and geographical ranges are shaped by these processes and how they shift under environmental change. Niche dynamics, intraspecific variability and the ability of species to track changing conditions are central questions.
